summary.intent: Design and spec out three memory-loop features: memory editing (title/body/keywords), keyword-based injection boosting, and a configurable generation threshold with named presets.
summary.outcome: A fully refined spec was written to docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-03-memory-loop-edit-keywords-threshold-design.md after three adversarial review rounds, an implementation plan was created in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-03-memory-loop-edit-keywords-threshold.md, and Task 1 (ParseKeywords + countMatchedKeywords) was dispatched to a subagent.

repo: Memory-loop generation pipeline filters candidates via three independent gates: evidence session count, confidence/strength floor, and generic advice phrase matching
Fingerprint for reconciliation is computed as FingerprintForRecord(kind, title, body) — keywords are intentionally excluded from the fingerprint
The huh library is used for interactive TUI form prompts throughout the wizard; force=true must be passed in tests to bypass TTY hangs
Singleton policy in the evidence gate was previously a bool but needs to be a tri-state string ('all', 'review-rules', 'none') to express balanced preset behavior
confidenceRank already exists in generator.go and returns ordered integers (low=1, medium=2, high=3), enabling comparison-based confidence filtering

code.finding: confidenceLow rejection gate — filters records where confidence == confidenceLow, equivalent to confidenceRank(confidence) < confidenceRank('medium')
confidenceRank function returns low=1, medium=2, high=3 — used to confirm behavioral equivalence when migrating to comparison-based threshold check
renderContentCard is where keywords display section needs to be added as Task 10
Wizard has existing suppress/archive actions; new WizardIntentEdit and edit stages need to be added alongside them
Settings tab is where threshold chip selector and override indicator (e.g. 'balanced*') will be added

workflow: Adversarial Codex review used to stress-test specs before implementation — three passes caught multi-word tokenization flaw, singleton bool limitation, missing override validation, and missing edit history previous-value capture
Design decisions locked down through explicit Q&A (pros/cons per option) before any spec writing, preventing spec rewrites
Subagent-driven development pattern used for implementation: one subagent per task, orchestrator reviews between tasks
Self-review checklist run after spec write catches placeholder scan, internal consistency, scope, and ambiguity before handing off to adversarial review

friction: Codex companion script hit ENOBUFS buffer overflow when run against the working tree due to large binary files (insights.db) and many untracked files — had to fall back to an Agent-based adversarial review instead

Keyword tokenization design required a mid-spec correction: initial AND-token approach was flawed (would match 'go test' keyword against any prompt containing 'test'), needed to be redefined as exact case-insensitive phrase/substring matching
open_items: Tasks 2-14 of the implementation plan are unstarted — only Task 1 (ParseKeywords + countMatchedKeywords) was dispatched to a subagent
SIGINT during $EDITOR leaves a stale temp file — spec notes this as a known acceptable limitation (same as git) but no cleanup code planned

Keywords on generated memories create a reconciliation fingerprint divergence scenario (user adds keywords → generator updates memory with new fingerprint → old version with keywords gets orphaned) — documented in spec but resolution deferred to implementation
